notes: I couldn't open any page. The Exeter grants URL and the internal and commercial pricing URLs all returned HTTP 404 to WebFetch. The 404 could mean the URLs moved, or that the site blocks the fetcher. I could not tell which, and I didn't reach an archive copy. The two searches gave only snippets. No Edinburgh, Liverpool CGR, Earlham, Oxford, Leeds or Birmingham costing page appeared. The one UK price list the search showed is Exeter's, and it carries no date. Because I never opened it, I can't confirm the 6000 vs X platform split, FEC rates or the page date. The search summary describes NovaSeq X 10B pricing, while the task brief says Exeter still runs a 6000.
how_to_mine: Try the Wayback Machine at web.archive.org for exeter.ac.uk/research/facilities/sequencing/pricing/internal and /commercial, because the two live URL variants both returned 404. Look for the page date and for any NovaSeq 6000 line items next to the X lines. Then search each UK core by name for its price list: Edinburgh Genomics (genomics.ed.ac.uk), Liverpool CGR (cgr.liv.ac.uk), Earlham Institute, Oxford WHG, Leeds, Birmingham (Genomics), Sanger and Glasgow Polyomics. Convert GBP to USD at the page date. Compare with Novogene UK quotes and with a 2024 or 2025 archived version to get a trend. The Exeter 10B flow cell price (about £14,400) is close to Illumina's published 10B-300 list price of $14,493, so check whether UK cores pass list price through without discount.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Exeter's internal UK price for an X 10B lane is £1,800 and its commercial price is £2,016, only about 12% higher. This suggests the facility passes Illumina list pricing through with little academic discount.
items.detail: This comes from a search-result snippet I could not open or date. Exeter's pricing page lists a single NovaSeq X 10B 300-cycle lane at £1,800 internal and £2,016 commercial, a 1.5B flow cell at £3,605, and a 10B flow cell at £14,400, all excluding VAT. £14,400 is close to Illumina's $14,493 10B-300 list price, so this looks like a pass-through. That would be the price ceiling UK researchers budget against. If cheaper vendors undercut it, research work leaves Illumina cores.
items.source_name: University of Exeter Sequencing Service (search snippet)
items.why_new: No UK core price list is in the known set, and the UK core sources used so far were procurement tenders.
